(Zyn, do you just lurk on the Recent Posts page and leap in with relevant links/info when you see somebody asking for help, like a superhero with extremely specific priorities?)

Creidieki, one issue is that a lot of Foundation lore is ambiguous, and is interpreted different ways by different authors. "Does the black moon howl?" has been used as a motto, a passcode prompt, a key concept in an SCP-001 entry, and many more besides. The only real common thread is that it's spooky and mysterious, and somehow associated with the Foundation. Having a clear reference for this sort of thing can be a bit tricky!

I tried to write this article such that even if you're not super familiar with Foundation lore, you can pick up enough from context clues to get the gist. The Ethics Committee is exactly what it says on the tin, for example. or is it?probablyhmmmdon't worry about it.

Anyway, the Foundation can be pretty lore-dense sometimes, but I hope you still enjoyed the article!

item.title: Re: Idea to prevent covid (In the SCP universe that is)
item.content:encoded:
Given the extremely negative responses to recent attempts to write up the COVID pandemic as an anomaly, it's probably not a good idea to encourage people do so. Members of the SCP wiki community have lost loved ones to coronavirus; attributing that very real life tragedy to a fictionalized anomalous version can come off as incredibly tactless.

exorbiant amounts

I think you mean "exorbitant", and there's a sentence in here that has a repeated "might". Just Ctrl+F for "might" and you'll find it. Beyond that, I think the dialogue portrayed here is a bit outside what someone would put in their seminar, I think people would rather just summarize the information that was said instead of writing out people as if they're characters. For example:

"So, what comes out of the door?" I asked, feeling the doorframe with my fingertips.

This is prose. In a summary of events, someone would probably write instead:

So I asked them what came out of the door.

Then the rest of that interaction could be summed by something like: "They told me that nothing comes out of the door, but that it opened to a dark ages cathedral in another dimension, housing a community of communist flower people."

Stuff like that. But, besides these gripes, I like this. It's cute, in a kind of way. I feel like if you followed this researcher around in episodic fashion, the tone would be that he always keeps his head, in a kind of lackadaisical sense where he doesn't ever feel too much in danger, and always safely makes it out while chaos collapses in around him. +1 because I like that tone, and the ending line got a chuckle.

item.title: Re: Fireproof Rescue Dog
item.content:encoded:
Hello BreakerBreaker! lets take a look :)

+ show block
– hide block

Concept:

This SCP is a former SAR (Search and Rescue) dog that is completely unaffected by fire and smoke. When irritated, the dog is also able to raise its internal body temperature to an unnaturally high level, allowing it to essentially burn those who come into contact with it. Visually, the dog is a completely average looking dalmatian. Given that it was an SAR animal, the dog had a handler. However, the handler was entirely non-anomalous and the dog’s anomalous protection did not extend to them nor anything other than itself.

Overall I think this is solid, my one concern here is its purpose. While it has a strong motive, there doesn't seem to be much of a reason for it exist in the first place, which (at least for me) takes some of my focus away from the narrative, as I'm continually asking myself "why".

- that said, this is a fairly minor issue, as the narrative isn't centred around that aspect.

Narrative:

The central narrative of this SCP Article would be the history of the SCP’s life prior to containment. This would be told through SAR incident reports recovered by the Foundation, detailing calls the dog was used on and how the dog and it’s handler performed. The reports would be written by the dog’s handler and would detail their specific experiences working with the dog during the incident.

I mainly second Cybersqyd here.

The dog is contained by the Foundation after it gives several children second and third degree burns. This result is from the dog spitting on and biting the children when they irritated it.

This incident is what alerts the Foundation to the dog’s existence. The dog is subsequently contained, with it’s handler and any witnesses to the incident anesthetized.

The article would end several years after the dog is contained, with a researcher in charge of the animal noting its declining health and mental state. The researcher makes a request to their superiors to suggest the dog be used for SAR work once again, this time for the Foundation. This portion of the article is told through an email.

Overall this sounds fairly solid too, my only real question; why didn't the Foundation see if they could utilise the dog earlier? considering they know about its history, and its general behaviour. It sounds like they would've at least tried at some points to use it for something. Rather than (assumably), continually keeping it locked away.- what was their reason for doing so?

A lot of the narrative will be dependant on how its executed, and the concept overall is workable. With that in mind, here is your second GreenLight..

Cheers,

RED

My review from the Art Exchange forum:

This is a fantastic article about a semi-Fifthist artifact's interactions with a Viatnamese uprising against French rule in the late 1930s. It's pretty amazing how much detail the author went into, and it's extra amazing how much character he wrote in. You can feel the love for history here. It's not just an interesting conflict in its own right, but it talks about how information gets recorded in the first place, carrying a theme of "your version of the truth", between how the Japanese interacted with the rock, the American talked about his view of the Vietnamese, and how the Vietnamese viewed the struggle, all with the central thematic piece of the pink rock which is "raw power", shaped by the wants and views of those who used it. It is an intimidatingly coherent piece with clear Lovecraftian inspiration (I know, I know, you can use "cosmic horror" to avoid attributing everything to direct Lovecraft inspiration nowadays but this is even set in the 1930s, you gotta realize that that's really contributing to the Lovecraft vibe here) as I always love to see in these Fifthist pieces. Good fucking job. One of the most solid creations for this art exchange.

I don't think I have anything to add. +1

I also agree that the plot point of "the Foundation just doesn't check their emails, ever" is bafflingly incompetent and just doesn't really make sense.

item.title: Re: -1
item.content:encoded:
Greetings. Let me go through this, as you've presented:

+ show block
– hide block

truly humanize Gabriel McQueen: The entirety of Addendum 1 was meant to do exactly this. In fact, a whopping majority of the article is spent characterizing McQueen, going into his personal life and his struggles growing up. I have no clue as to how else to characterize him without dumping thousands of more words into the article, causing it drag along moreso than it maybe has already.

a b-list slasher: since you don't necessarily state the criteria for this, I have no clue how to correct it. The log itself has already been reduced via the lack of sound, which was intended to subvert this problem. The only thing readers get to see is purely the visual feed, which in my opinion seems pretty realistic? I don't understand where it falls from feeling real to "being like a crappy film." I can almost see the mention of Laura in a bath towel being a potential source of the problem, so I have removed it. However, I would like to ask what you'd do in this situation presented? How could I detract it less from sounding like this?

walking mental-illness stereotype: Frankly I don't necessarily know where this stems from. The only part of McQueen where I could potentially see potential stereotyping is the mention of medication for anger-related problems. I have since removed this, but otherwise I'm unsure of where else this occurs. I tried as best as I could to keep mentions or anything of explicit mental health problems at a minimum to avoid this. As to the part where you mentioned that his killings were unjustified: I'd have to argue against this. Its hinted several times that McQueen was somewhat unstable, even directly admitting to torturing animals (which is an indication of underlying tendencies). Also, just logically speaking, how fast do you think you'd confront a cheating spouse? I feel as if it would be unrealistic to elongate McQueens confrontation, especially given the context that he had hidden cameras all over the house. In this regard, I simply have no solution.

multiple errors in grammar: These are being corrected, but currently I'm working ;-;

article devolves: I cite my earlier comment of the "b-slasher movie" to be vague. I simply don't understand nor know how to fix this. Not only that, but the contrast was intended ([…] that has changed a once innocuous place into something…else). I specifically wanted there to be a sharp contrast in order for the ending to be more surprising for the reader. But, still, this is a valid critique. I'm unsure of how to fix it though.

despite my expectations going in: this doesn't necessarily seem like a problem tied to the article. In truth, this seems a bit unfair. I have no way to defend against pre-conceived expectations, especially considering that this story wasn't meant to "awe-dropping." It was intended to be personal, to have an emotional connection amongst a small group of people. In my opinion, downvoting an article based off prior expectations seems somewhat unreasonable. (This isn't to suggest that that's what you did, just in general)

I really do appreciate your comments. I will try to address them in a decent manner. I'll edit this comment once they've been implemented. Thank you!

item.title: Re: Dysphoric Flesh
item.content:encoded:
I feel like I should put something here and uh I have now nice

[+] Overall
[-] Overall

I’m…not sure about this as a whole. My central concern is that the way the notes plays out feels…predictable? The emotional beats within are like, not badly done but they are done in a way that just kinda feels very expected?

The ending stands out as odd: the survival of Leif isn’t necessarily bad but it kinda, feels unimpactful in a way I can’t quite put my finger on? I think it’s because post the notes, there’s nothing really like, establishing that they might be dead: the ‘originally assumed to be a suicide note’ implies it isn’t, which in turn implies they aren’t dead, so there’s no like, stomach drop ‘are they…are they dead’ followed by subversion when they aren’t. Technically the discovery section opens with the implication they are dead but it feels like this needs a callback to that first before it can be subverted for the emotions to hit: like, if the suicide note was found and there was mention of a funeral say, there was some…minor thing to allow the emotions to hit, and then the discovery of them being found?

Even then, the relatively pedestrian nature of the notes might be an issue; but it’s possible this is just me having read too many scps and being generally jaded as a whole rather than an actual issue: if you’re getting positive feedback on this, it’s probably fine?

[-] Overall
[+] Line By Line
[-] Line By Line

Gonna note that I can miss stuff; flag things which are right as being wrong and indeed flag things which are deliberately wrong.
I'll likely use strikethrough to indicate stuff to remove and green text to indicate stuff to add.

Subjects believed to be instances of SCP-XXXX-2 are to be re-located to Foundation emergency clinics immediately for evaluation.

Probably stylistic largely, but it feels like having ‘immediately’ right before ‘re-located’ instead would be clearer

Center subject is SCP-XXXX-2-C33, infected with an instance of SCP-XXXX. Subject furthest right is SCP-XXXX-1-C33.

This feels over long for a caption; I think the ‘infected with…SCP-XXXX’ part could be trimmed; and maybe the rest streamlined further? Though I’m not sure how easy that’d be.

Contact with SCP-XXXX-1 is to be allowed once a day for feeding purposes.

The implication to me of ‘contact’ here is ‘foundation contact’, but it seems like you mean ‘SCP-XXXX-2 contact’ and I feel like it could do with being more explicit?

If SCP-XXXX-1 cannot be used

I’m not exactly sure why but something about this doesn’t sit right with me; I’m not sure if it’s the kinda casual writing or the vagueness about why -1 couldn’t be used or what though.

SCP-XXXX eggs are summoned directly into the womb, causing the subject to become an instance of SCP-XXXX-1.

‘summoned’ feels…strangely purposeful at this point: like, summoning usually implies there’s a summoner doing it; and it feels…like an angle which never really ends up going anywhere?

It then makes its way to offspring of SCP-XXXX-1 in an approximately 200-meter radius.

I guess my question is ‘what if no-such offspring are within a 200m radius?’

SCP-XXXX will attach itself to transgender or non-binary offspring of SCP-XXXX-1, hereby referred to as SCP-XXXX-2.

I feel like this should be like…next to the previous thing about it travelling to offspring? Like, if the sentence was like “It then travels to transgender or non-binary offspring of SCP-XXXX-1 in an approximately 200m radius” say.

SCP-XXXX is considered to have entered its adult phase.
In adult SCP-XXXX instances

I’d probably be consistent as to whether this is an ‘adult phase’ or ‘adult SCP-XXXX instances’; though the repetition might feel iffy: perhaps ‘These instances…’ would be fine to start the second with?

the memetic camouflage agent changes in function. SCP-XXXX will utilize its illusory effect to conceal itself and to modify SCP-XXXX-2’s appearance.

I would probably shorten this into one sentence.

Trans-positive cultural attitudes surrounding SCP-XXXX-2 have also been liked to the incidence of SCP-XXXX death.

I…don’t dislike this as a statement or anything but it raises the question of why the Foundation aren’t like…doing more to promote trans positivity? Like it’s the kinda thing you mention offhandedly here that makes me question why there’s not a co-ordinated propaganda effort to increase trans-positivity as a containment procedure for SCP-XXXX but *shrugs*

Foundation personnel were summoned to investigate the circumstances surrounding the death of Leif Ivanovich (20) in Eugene, OR.

This feels kinda weirdly passive: who summoned the Foundation? Why did they summon the Foundation?

[-] Line By Line

item.title: Idea for Greenlight - Russian Nesting Souls
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Page Layout (Optional): Standard layout + Incident/testing/interview logs

Elevator Pitch:
SCP-XXXX is a Russian nesting doll consisting of 3 layers. Upon opening the innermost doll; the object will activate. Upon activation, the 5 meter radius around the doll will be filled with a bright piercing light of no discernible origin for about 30 seconds. During this time, all individuals in area aside from the object's activator (henceforth SCP-XXXX-1) will immediately be vaporized. SCP-XXXX-1 will find themselves transfigured into one the now missing individuals, both in look and voice. The doll will now be embedded in the center of their chest with the front side protruding. Doll will now depict separate individual who was vaporized. Upon death or attempted removal of doll (which will cause instant heart failure), XXXX-1 will transfigure into individual depicted on doll, and the doll will change to depict a new individual. The entity will then come back to life. This process continues until all iterations have been cycled through and the entity will return to their original body; with the doll now depicting it's original marking. Any death or attempted removal after this point will result in permanent death at which object will dislodge itself. The object can speak telepathically to XXXX-1 and does so in a motherly Russian voice.

Central Narrative:
Through logs, the article will detail an incident during initial testing in which a D-class activated the object, resulting in the absorption of 2 researchers, an agent, a janitor, and another D-class. Further testing of object will be detailed as well as interviews with object will be noted. Ultimately, site directors decide object is safer contained in vessel as re-activation would require vessel be killed multiple times. Most knowledge of object is candidly provided by object itself in interviews. Object appears to have been created as a tool of war.

Hook/Attention-Grabber:
I plan to weave a narrative of the D-class who has essentially became a living nesting doll, now with multiple "lives".

Additional Notes: I am aware of two other nesting doll SCP, so hopefully 3 isn't a crowd. The anomalous effects of the object should be fresh enough though.

item.title: Re: Blood Rose
item.content:encoded:
+Show block
-hide block

This feels…kinda edgy and also a little insensitive towards folk who self harm;

I was trying to go for a slightly horrifying feeling; You're right, it does sound a little insensitive to anyone who self-harms. If it seems edgy because of that fact then maybe something else like, "it causes anyone to spontaneously bleed as they get nearer." Maybe the smell of the rose compels them to get closer, and then they start to bleed as they get nearer; and the longer the rose goes without blood, the more intoxicating and dangerous it becomes.

but I think the bigger issue is that the compulsion effect means you're removing a lot of the opportunity to explore why someone would choose to water the flower with blood.

You mention in the hook that the flower contains 'the history of all it's victims': maybe there's an interesting historical angle you could take this on then? Like, perhaps if the flower was considered a holy object or something and people worshipped it and were affected by it to a lesser extent and then gradually it got more powerful or something.

That's a really good idea, actually. I did think that this concept could go several different ways. Maybe a ritual someone was performing to bring someone else back to life, and it went wrong or something, and all the bodies in the hill were past victims. As for the historical part this whole thing could go back hundreds of years: every few years someone comes across the rose and dies, anything they had on them at the time tells how long ago it was. The DNA part might need some work too.

I read SCP-3597 and the way the containment process went might work for this, though it would be a bit different. It seemed based on a visual cognitohazard, whereas this is a smell cognitohazard.

So how about this instead:
The Foundation find a journal buried in the hill the rose is on. In it is the story of a man and his dead
lover. He tries to bring her back to life using a dark ritual. It yields a rose that reminds him of her, but he feels compelled to water it with human blood. He kills a few people for their blood before he starts to use his own blood to water it. He eventually goes insane and kills himself. But the rose still remains. Anyone who happens upon it is enamored by it's beauty and intoxicated by it's smell, and they end up bleeding to death when they try to get near it. So the foundation has a bit of trouble containing it, and they end up building a containment unit around it, and it grows into a massive thorn bush, but it stays contained.

I appreciate you feedback. Thank you for taking the time to look this all over.

item.title: Re: Semi-Veil breaking Parawatch SCP idea
item.content:encoded:
Brought here on request, lets take a look.

Looking at the SCP itself, it seems fairly simple and straightforward. However, it may be a bit too simplistic? It falls under a thing that does a thing in my mind, a photo that when copied makes frogs appear. If that's the extent of what the SCP does, I suggest adding a bit more depth to it unless you can really pull off the comedy aspect of it. Even then, if you try that angle it may be wise to try and head down the route of a tale instead.

The narrative seems to have groundwork laid, but needs additional work. I'm really not sure how this frog picture almost breaks the veil as outlined. The Foundation lists Parawatch as a group that poses little threat to secrecy and the veil, and is purposefully left alone to misinform the public on the paranormal. So, I would suggest editing the threat to the veil either be more concrete or really play into the comedy aspect of the article. At the moment, I see how it could be humorous but pulling off a comedy article can be tough not to make it cliche. Either way, the idea still could use some work. You have a good start, but for me the idea is too simple and doesn't fit in with what Parawatch can do. Best of luck.

item.title: Re: Staff Post - Deletion Vote
item.content:encoded:
Two


Forum category: Per Page Discussions / Per page discussions
Forum thread: SCP-5188

This really did very little for me, despite my expectations going in. The central story behind this article is one that's been told many, many times before — and this article didn't delve any deeper into it than any other stories have in the past. I see no attempt here to truly humanize Gabriel McQueen — he's just a walking mental-illness stereotype whose descent into murderous frenzy is never really built up or justified until a paragraph before shit goes down. The scenes of incredible violence in this are all too gratuitous and over-the-top to take seriously, and the actions and behaviour of McQueen in those scenes are reminiscent of a b-list slasher movie.

Also an issue for me are the multiple errors in grammar (for example - the apostrophe in "lifts" in "McQueen lift's Laura"), style (always referring to characters by their first names in the recording logs), and the choppy and somewhat stilted structure of the syntax, which along with the over-the-top scenes of unnecessary and graphic violence made this hard to get through.

Lastly (and this may not be up to me to decide, but it's only my opinion), the content of this article seems to sharply contrast with the initial prompt behind it. While the initial anomaly of the article follows the subtlety and quiet emotion suggested by the prompt quite well, it quickly becomes an afterthought as the story of the article devolves into a slasher movie in SCP form.

I started reading this article expecting something incredible, and left sorely disappointed. Downvote.

item.title: Re: DECEMBER 2020 INTROS - Writers
item.content:encoded:
Hey Alias Copernicus, and welcome! You'd be surprised just how many people join the site like yourself. They spend a long time reading from it but not joining till much later. But, we are glad you decided to join. Being a fan of mystery should be like a gold mine here, there are so many articles I've read that just leave me wondering. Make sure to take your time and get acquainted with how everything here works, and make sure to check out IRC chat too!

For my recommendation, you should check out SCP-5699

+ Resources
- Hide Resources

For posting ideas, make sure you go through the proper greenlighting process on the idea forums first. Remember that there is no rush, and you should take time familiarizing yourself with how Series 6 articles are formatted. We are a rather unique bunch so I'm sure just reading and being a part of the community will be rather fun for you!

If you're going to try your hand at writing, try out our sandbox. You can make yourself a page here to store your drafts.

Sandbox

For hashing out concepts, try out the Ideas and Brainstorming forum. You can run your ideas by the community if you need help refining your concept.

If you have a draft ready, make a thread in the Drafts and Critiques forum. Remember to check the stickied posts in the relevant thread for guidelines on how best to use each forum. You can also try the IRC chat for real-time feedback.

From site usage to writing tips, the Guide Hub contains a wealth of resources geared towards helping members produce successful articles.

The more time you take to familiarize yourself with the SCP style, the drafting process, and the community, the greater your chances are for success!

As far as reading is concerned, you might want to check out our Top Rated New Pages, which will display the most popular, recent articles. It's helpful to keep up with what's being received well by the community.


Best of luck!
